---
title: "Frames from border bands"
subtitle: "Four sides that mirror exactly, and three ways to turn the corner"
---

## In plain words

A frame is four border bands around an empty middle. Each side is made of whole
repeats of a band from the book, plus one extra column when the band needs it,
so every side is an exact mirror image of itself end to end. The band's top
row faces outwards on all four sides.

Where two sides meet there is a square as tall as the band. That corner is
where the new design happens, and there are three ways to fill it:

| Corner | How it is made |
|---|---|
| **Mitre** | Both bands run on into the corner and meet on the diagonal, like a picture frame. Because the sides end on a mirror line, the seam is exact. |
| **Motif block** | A small motif from the same manuscript, symmetric across the diagonal, is set in the corner square. |
| **Grown** | The mitre is drawn, a disc in its middle is cleared, and the fill method grows new pattern there from the band. It is mirrored across the diagonal, and a seed fixes it. |

**Cut.** A repeat can be started at any column, but the sides only mirror
exactly at the band's own mirror lines. *Best cut*, the default, tries every
cut that mirrors and keeps the one with the cleanest corner: the fewest stray
stitches of 1 to 3 cells, then the shortest float. *Stored cut* uses the cut
from the Sjónabók repository.

Every frame below is as wide as fits on the machine (179 needles).

## Make one yourself

```sh
make frame BAND=thjms1105_38_p2 NX=4 NY=3 CORNER=all SEED=1
```

This writes `frame.png`, `frame-grid.png`, `frame.txt` and `frame.meta.json`
for each corner type, and `corners.png` with them side by side.

## Good at, weak at

| Good at | Weak at |
|---|---|
| Exact mirrored sides from any band with a mirror line (196 of 290 repeat units) | Bands without a mirror line cannot make a frame this way |
| The mitre needs no new design and always joins cleanly | The grown corner can look busy: the fill method only learns from one band |
| A frame is small enough to knit as a test piece | Small bands (10 to 12 rows) have no motif small enough for a motif block |
